data.sentence: Thanks for making time, Raymond, Linda. I've got a short deck, but I'd rather make this a conversation.
Let's start where we started in February — your backup environment across the two data centers and the cloud workloads.
Sure. All four hundred and fifty on-prem VMs are now on Protect, and we finished the DICOM imaging archive migration two weeks ago.
That was the big one, two hundred terabytes, and it went more smoothly than I expected.
That's great. And the recovery testing — that was your biggest concern back then.
We ran our first full DR test last month. Our target recovery time for the EHR system was four hours and we recovered in two hours and fifty minutes.
That's the first time in five years we've had a tested recovery time I can actually put in front of our board.
That's exactly the outcome we were aiming for. Congratulations to your team.
I'll be honest, after the API outage in February I wasn't sure we'd get here.
Three days without backup orchestration on patient data was not a good start to the relationship.
I remember, and I appreciate you sticking with us through that.
Priya handled it well. And the SIEM connector issue from February has been clean since the fix — no gaps in LogVault since March.
Let's talk about what's next. Raymond, you mentioned storage costs on the imaging archive.
Yes. Most of the DICOM data is rarely read after ninety days, but it all sits on the standard tier.
If we could move older studies to a cold tier automatically, I think we'd cut storage cost by a third.
Protect supports lifecycle policies to an archive tier. I can have our solutions team model the savings using your actual access patterns.
That would be really useful for our budget cycle in August.
The bigger ask from me is multi-region replication. We're opening a third site in Sacramento and I want a copy outside the Bay Area.
That's on the Protect roadmap for Q3. I'll get you a firmer date and see if you can join the early access program.
Please. If it slips past Q3, we'll need to build something ourselves, and I'd rather not.
Understood. One more thing — you're using Comply for HIPAA. How has v2 been?
Good. The on-demand HIPAA report saved my compliance team a lot of evidence gathering, and the Protect recovery tests show up as evidence automatically.
Would it be worth a conversation about Detect at some point? It would feed into the same evidence trail.
Maybe later this year. After what happened in March, I want to see a few clean quarters before I put threat monitoring on you as well.
That's completely fair. I'll share the reliability updates as they come, with no pressure.
Can you send the deck and the cost model when it's ready?
Yes, the deck today, and the archive cost model within two weeks.
Thanks, Lisa. This was a good review — it's nice to have one of these that's mostly good news.
